name: Plasma frequency as photon mass for axion resonance
summary: In a plasma the photon acquires an effective mass ħω_p, so axion–photon (and dark-photon) conversion is resonant where m_a c² = ħω_p. This underlies radio-line searches for axion dark matter converting in neutron-star magnetospheres, tunable plasma haloscopes that set ω_p with wire metamaterials, and resonant dark-photon production in the Sun. Stellar-plasma emission (Primakoff, plasmon decay) is also behind stellar-cooling bounds on axions and neutrino dipole moments.

name: Hypermagnetic helicity, the anomaly and inverse cascades
summary: Above the electroweak scale, helical hypercharge magnetic fields source baryon and lepton number through the U(1)_Y anomaly. Their evolution (the inverse helicity cascade in MHD turbulence and helicity decay at the electroweak crossover) can therefore generate or wash out the baryon asymmetry (Giovannini–Shaposhnikov 1998; Kamada–Long 2016).

name: Sphaleron rate set by hot gauge-plasma kinetics
summary: Baryon-violating sphaleron transitions in the hot electroweak plasma run through soft magnetic modes (k ~ g²T) that hard particles overdamp via Landau damping. Arnold–Son–Yaffe and Bödeker showed Γ_sph ∝ α_w^5 T^4 ln(1/α_w); Bödeker's effective theory is a Langevin equation equivalent to Ohmic magnetic diffusion with a colour conductivity. Plasma kinetics thus fixes the rate used in baryogenesis and washout calculations.

name: Dark plasmas: instabilities constrain charged dark matter
summary: If dark matter carries charge under a dark U(1) or a millicharge, halos behave as collisionless plasmas. In cluster mergers, Weibel and two-stream instabilities could isotropize and decelerate dark matter far faster than binary scattering, so plasma growth rates rather than cross-sections set Bullet-Cluster-type bounds on the dark fine-structure constant.
breaks: Whether the instabilities grow and saturate fast enough to transfer momentum is contested; later analyses argued earlier bounds were overestimated. Magnetized dark plasmas also behave differently.

name: Bullet Cluster: plasma shock versus collisionless DM
summary: In the merging Bullet Cluster (1E 0657-56) ram pressure slows the X-ray intracluster plasma, which drives a Mach ≈ 3 bow shock, while the lensing mass passes through with the galaxies. The offset is key evidence for collisionless particle dark matter and bounds its self-interaction. The same shock is a laboratory for collisionless-shock physics and electron–ion equilibration.

name: Parker bound: galactic dynamo limits GUT monopoles
summary: Grand unification predicts superheavy 't Hooft–Polyakov monopoles. Monopoles crossing the Galaxy would be accelerated by its magnetic field and drain its energy faster than the galactic dynamo regenerates it (~10^8 yr), which gives the Parker bound on the monopole flux. This dynamo constraint on GUT cosmology, together with the monopole overabundance problem, helped motivate inflation.
sources: Georgi & Glashow (1974). "Unity of All Elementary-Particle Forces". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 32, 438. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.438](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.438)
Parker (1955). "Hydromagnetic Dynamo Models". *Astrophys. J.* 122, 293. [doi:10.1086/146087](https://doi.org/10.1086/146087)

name: g−2 from cyclotron versus spin precession
summary: The muon g−2 storage ring (BNL, Fermilab) measures ω_a = ω_s − ω_c, the beat between spin precession and cyclotron gyration in a uniform 1.45 T field. It uses electrostatic quadrupole focusing and the magic momentum 3.09 GeV/c (γ ≈ 29.3), which cancels the β×E term. Electron g−2 uses one electron in a Penning trap, whose magnetron motion is the E×B drift: single-particle orbit theory as a precision instrument.

name: Laser and beam plasmas as advanced-accelerator R&D
summary: The laser–plasma toolkit (chirped-pulse-amplified lasers, beam–plasma interaction, plasma lenses, wakefield staging) is the advanced-accelerator line in collider strategy studies, and collider luminosity targets translate back into required driver average power, kHz repetition rates and wall-plug efficiency for the plasma community.
sources: Esarey, Schroeder & Leemans (2009). "Physics of laser-driven plasma-based electron accelerators". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 1229. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.81.1229](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.81.1229)

name: Beamstrahlung and laser radiation reaction share χ
summary: At linear-collider interaction points the collective field of one nanometre-scale bunch acts on the other like an ultra-intense laser. Particles pinch (disruption), radiate (beamstrahlung) and convert photons to pairs, governed by the same quantum-nonlinearity parameter χ (Υ) that defines the radiation-reaction and QED-plasma regime of multi-PW laser–plasma experiments. Beam–beam codes and QED-PIC codes use the same locally-constant-field emission rates.

name: Plasma wakefield accelerators as compact collider drivers
summary: Plasma waves sustain accelerating fields near the cold wave-breaking limit, 10–100 GV/m against ~100 MV/m in RF cavities, so laser- or beam-driven wakefield stages are the candidate route to compact multi-TeV lepton colliders; collider requirements (energy spread, emittance preservation, wall-plug efficiency, positron acceleration, staging) define the field's open problems.
sources: Tajima & Dawson (1979). "Laser Electron Accelerator". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 43, 267. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.267](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.267)
Litos et al. (2014). "High-efficiency acceleration of an electron beam in a plasma wakefield accelerator". *Nature* 515, 92. [doi:10.1038/nature13882](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature13882)

name: High-field superconducting magnets: colliders and tokamaks
summary: Collider energy scales as B·R and tokamak fusion power at fixed β as B^4, so both push the same conductors. These are Nb–Ti (LHC, 8.3 T), Nb3Sn (HL-LHC triplets ~11 T, ITER toroidal-field and central-solenoid coils) and REBCO high-temperature superconductors (the 20 T CFS/MIT SPARC model coil, 2021; candidate FCC-hh dipoles and muon-collider solenoids). Both fields share quench protection, stress management and cryogenics.

name: AWAKE: proton-driven wakefields from the LHC injectors
summary: AWAKE at CERN sends 400 GeV SPS proton bunches (the LHC injector beam) into a 10 m rubidium plasma; the bunch, far longer than λ_p, undergoes the seeded self-modulation instability into microbunches that resonantly drive a wake, which accelerated injected electrons to ~2 GeV (2018). Proton bunches store ~20–130 kJ, enough in principle for single-stage acceleration to TeV energies.

name: Electron cloud and two-stream instability in the LHC
summary: Synchrotron-light photoelectrons multiply by secondary emission into an electron cloud in the LHC beam screen. This non-neutral plasma adds cryogenic heat load and drives the electron–proton two-stream instability, tune shifts and emittance growth. It is analysed with plasma linear-instability theory and particle-in-cell codes, and mitigated by beam scrubbing and low-secondary-yield coatings.

name: Hillas criterion: cosmic accelerators versus colliders
summary: Any accelerator must keep the particle's gyroradius inside the accelerating region, so maximum energy scales as field times size. 8.33 T dipoles on a 2.8 km bending radius give the LHC 7 TeV, while the Hillas criterion applied to supernova-remnant, AGN-jet and cluster shocks bounds cosmic-ray energies up to ~10^20 eV (√s ≈ 430 TeV on a proton target).
breaks: Shock acceleration is stochastic: repeated diffusive crossings in turbulent, self-generated fields produce power-law spectra, and β_s≪1 plus radiative or escape losses lower E_max. Colliders accelerate coherently with RF in fixed guide fields and deliver near-monoenergetic beams.
sources: Blandford & Ostriker (1978). "Particle acceleration by astrophysical shocks". *Astrophys. J.* 221, L29. [doi:10.1086/182658](https://doi.org/10.1086/182658)

name: Jet quenching as stopping power in a QCD plasma
summary: Energy loss of a fast parton crossing the QGP is computed like charged-particle stopping in a plasma. It has three parts: collisional loss with a Coulomb logarithm cut off by the Debye mass (Bjorken 1982; Braaten–Thoma), a jet transport coefficient q̂ that is a transverse-momentum (Fokker–Planck) diffusion coefficient, and radiative loss with Landau–Pomeranchuk–Migdal coherence (BDMPS).
breaks: For coloured partons radiative loss dominates and grows as L² (BDMPS). Non-relativistic plasma stopping has no counterpart, since bremsstrahlung there is negligible.

name: Machine learning for triggers and tokamak control
summary: HEP developed low-latency deep learning for triggers, fast surrogate simulation and anomaly detection; fusion has its counterparts in neural disruption predictors (Kates-Harbeck et al. 2019) and reinforcement-learning magnetic control on TCV (Degrave et al. 2022). Both need microsecond-scale FPGA inference, rare-event detection under class imbalance, and simulation-trained models that survive domain shift to the real machine.

name: Gaseous detectors are controlled Townsend discharges
summary: Geiger and proportional counters, MWPCs, drift chambers, GEMs, Micromegas and RPCs amplify ionization by Townsend avalanches. They must stay below the Raether limit (αd ≈ 20, ~10^8 electrons), where avalanches become streamers and sparks; this is the breakdown physics of gas discharges (Townsend coefficients, Paschen curves, streamer theory). RPCs run deliberately in avalanche or streamer mode, and detector ageing is plasma polymerization, the same chemistry as plasma deposition.

name: Geiger counters discovered the radiation belts
summary: Van Allen's Geiger–Müller counters on Explorer 1 and 3 (1958) saturated in trapped-particle regions, which is how the radiation belts were discovered. Space-plasma particle instruments descend from nuclear and particle detectors (scintillators, silicon, magnetic spectrometers such as AMS-02). LHC front-end electronics and satellites face the same single-event effects and radiation-hardness engineering.

name: Shock-accelerated cosmic rays as neutrino sources
summary: Diffusive shock acceleration gives power-law protons whose pp and pγ collisions make pions. Pion decays yield neutrinos carrying ~5% of the proton energy, with flavor ratio ≈1:1:1 at Earth and a spectrum that tracks the parent. This is the hadronic-source signature IceCube seeks (TXS 0506+056, the Galactic plane), although coronal sources such as NGC 1068 may accelerate by turbulence or reconnection instead.
sources: Blandford & Ostriker (1978). "Particle acceleration by astrophysical shocks". *Astrophys. J.* 221, L29. [doi:10.1086/182658](https://doi.org/10.1086/182658)

name: MSW potential and plasma frequency: medium dispersion
summary: Coherent forward scattering on electrons gives electron neutrinos the potential V = √2 G_F n_e (Wolfenstein 1978), just as forward scattering of photons on free electrons gives the refractive term ω_p² ∝ n_e. Both shift the dispersion in proportion to electron density, and resonant MSW level crossings (adiabatic or Landau–Zener) parallel mode conversion at resonances in inhomogeneous plasmas.
breaks: The MSW potential is a flavor-dependent weak-interaction effect (~10^-11 eV in the solar core) that acts through mixing rather than giving a mass or cutoff. Photon refraction is electromagnetic and produces a cutoff at ω = ω_p.
sources: Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)

name: Neutrino quantum kinetics as matrix-valued Vlasov
summary: Neutrino transport with oscillations obeys quantum kinetic equations (Sigl–Raffelt 1993) for flavor density matrices. They combine free streaming, a commutator with a self-consistent mean-field Hamiltonian (vacuum, MSW and ν–ν refraction) and collisions. This is the structure of a Vlasov system with a self-consistent field, so mean-field, quasilinear and moment-closure methods transfer from plasma kinetics.

abla+\mathbf a\cdot
abla_{\mathbf v})f=0
breaks: There is no momentum-space force term: refraction rotates flavor instead of accelerating particles. The nonlinearity is a flavor-space commutator rather than a velocity-space one.

name: Fast flavor instability from plasma dispersion relations
summary: In supernova cores and neutron-star mergers, neutrino–neutrino forward scattering makes flavor evolution collective. Linearizing the off-diagonal flavor density matrix gives a dispersion relation whose complex roots signal the fast flavor instability, analysed like a beam–plasma instability (Izaguirre, Raffelt & Tamborra 2017). A crossing in the angular electron-lepton-number distribution plays the role of a bump-on-tail, and Landau-damping and quasilinear-saturation ideas carried over.

name: Chiral magnetic effect as an α-dynamo
summary: In a plasma with chiral imbalance μ_5 (early universe, proto-neutron stars, heavy-ion collisions) the anomaly drives a current along B: the chiral magnetic effect. This current enters the induction equation exactly like the mean-field α-effect, giving a chiral dynamo (chiral plasma instability) that amplifies helical fields while the anomaly drains μ_5 (Boyarsky, Fröhlich & Ruchayskiy 2012; Rogachevskii et al. 2017).
map: \mathbf J_{CME}=\frac{e^2\mu_5}{2\pi^2}\mathbf B;\quad \partial_t\mathbf B=\nabla\times(\mathbf v\times\mathbf B+\alpha_5\mathbf B)+\eta\nabla^2\mathbf B,\ \alpha_5\leftrightarrow\alpha
breaks: The classical α-effect is a statistical property of helical turbulence. The chiral α is microscopic, fixed by the anomaly coefficient, and decays as chirality-flipping (electron-mass) scattering erases μ_5 at low temperature.

name: Magnetic helicity is an abelian Chern–Simons term
summary: Magnetic helicity H = ∫A·B d³x is the abelian Chern–Simons functional. It measures the linking of field lines (Moffatt 1969) and is exactly conserved in ideal MHD because E·B = 0 (Woltjer 1958). Through the axial anomaly it trades with fermion chirality so that N_5 + (e²/4π²)H is conserved, the bridge behind chiral MHD and anomaly-driven baryogenesis.
map: H=\int\mathbf A\cdot\mathbf B\,d^3x,\quad \frac{dH}{dt}=-2\int\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B\,d^3x,\quad \partial_\mu j_5^\mu=\frac{e^2}{2\pi^2}\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B
breaks: Classical helicity is continuous and conserved only approximately (resistivity, reconnection). Non-abelian Chern–Simons number changes by integers between topologically distinct vacua via instantons and sphalerons.
sources: Adler (1969). "Axial-Vector Vertex in Spinor Electrodynamics". *Phys. Rev.* 177, 2426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426)

name: Field-theory action principles for Vlasov–Maxwell
summary: Vlasov–Maxwell is a classical field theory: Low (1958) gave its Lagrangian, and Morrison, Marsden and Weinstein gave its noncanonical Lie–Poisson Hamiltonian structure. Gyrokinetic field theories and structure-preserving variational particle-in-cell schemes derive from such actions, and Martin–Siggia–Rose functional integrals treat plasma-turbulence statistics with the generating-functional machinery of QFT.
breaks: The Vlasov bracket is noncanonical with Casimir invariants and is never quantized. MSR integrals weight stochastic histories, not quantum amplitudes.

name: Gyrokinetics as a scale-separated effective theory
summary: Gyrokinetics removes fast gyration (ω ≪ Ω_c) with a gyrophase-averaging Lie transform ordered in ρ* = ρ/L, keeps the magnetic moment as an adiabatic invariant, and adds corrections order by order. Structurally this is like integrating out a heavy scale in an EFT such as NRQED or HQET, with ρ* as the power-counting parameter.
breaks: Gyrokinetics is a classical asymptotic phase-space reduction with no loops, renormalization or running couplings. Its orderings (δf/f ~ ρ*) are imposed rather than symmetry-protected, and they fail in steep edge pedestals.

name: MHD as the effective theory of a one-form symmetry
summary: With no magnetic monopoles, magnetic flux conservation is a one-form global symmetry. Grozdanov, Hofman and Iqbal (2017) recast relativistic dissipative MHD as the hydrodynamic effective theory of that symmetry, organized by a derivative expansion with symmetry-allowed transport coefficients. Frozen-in flux and Alfvén waves then follow from symmetry plus EFT power counting.

name: Strong-field QED in the laser–plasma QED regime
summary: At intensities ≳10^23 W/cm² (a0 of a few hundred) plasma electrons reach χ ~ 1, where nonlinear Compton emission and multiphoton Breit–Wheeler pair creation dominate. Their rates are Feynman diagrams in the Furry picture with Volkov-dressed propagators, inserted as Monte Carlo processes in QED-PIC codes. SLAC E-144 first observed them in the 1990s, and Schwinger pair creation at E_S is the non-perturbative limit.

name: Debye-screened potential is the Yukawa potential
summary: A massive boson's static propagator 1/(k²+m²) Fourier-transforms to the Yukawa potential. A plasma's static longitudinal dielectric function ε(k)=1+1/(k²λ_D²) turns the Coulomb propagator into 1/(k²+λ_D⁻²), giving the same potential with λ_D in place of the Compton wavelength. Hence 'Yukawa systems' for dusty plasmas and the 'Debye mass' of thermal field theory.
breaks: Debye screening is a collective, temperature-dependent medium effect. It applies to static longitudinal fields only (static magnetic fields are unscreened), needs N_D≫1 for linearity, and has no associated free particle; the Yukawa range comes from the rest mass of a quantum exchanged in vacuum.

name: Renormalization group for MHD turbulence
summary: Field-theory machinery moved into turbulence theory. Wyld's diagrammatic expansion, Kraichnan-type renormalized closures and Wilsonian RG were applied to randomly forced MHD (Fournier, Sulem & Pouquet 1982) and to magnetized-plasma turbulence, yielding renormalized eddy viscosity and resistivity and infrared fixed points that set inertial-range exponents.
breaks: There is no small parameter (the ε-expansion is extrapolated to large ε), and mean-field anisotropy (critical balance) and intermittency are not captured.

name: Vacuum polarization as screening, asymptotic freedom
summary: A running coupling is a scale-dependent dielectric function. QED vacuum polarization by virtual pairs screens a bare charge so α grows at short distance, as a polarizable medium or plasma screens a test charge. In QCD, gluon self-interaction overcompensates (antiscreening), giving asymptotic freedom.
breaks: Plasma screening comes from real thermal charges and is exponential beyond λ_D. Vacuum screening is Lorentz-invariant, involves only virtual pairs and is merely logarithmic, so the charge is never fully screened. Equilibrium plasmas have no antiscreening counterpart.
sources: Gross & Wilczek (1973). "Ultraviolet Behavior of Non-Abelian Gauge Theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 30, 1343. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343)

name: Coulomb logarithm by dimensional regularization
summary: The Coulomb logarithm reflects a collision integral divergent at both ends: the Boltzmann binary-collision operator diverges at large impact parameter and the Lenard–Balescu collective operator at small. Brown, Preston and Singleton (2005) continued the kinetic equations to d dimensions (Boltzmann for d>3, Lenard–Balescu for d<3) and cancelled the poles at d=3 as in dimensional regularization. This fixes ln Λ, with its constant term, for stopping power and temperature equilibration.

name: Antimatter non-neutral plasmas enable CPT tests
summary: Antihydrogen for CPT-symmetry tests (ALPHA's 1S–2S line matches hydrogen to ~2×10⁻¹²) is made by merging antiproton and positron non-neutral plasmas in Penning–Malmberg traps. The process relies on one-component-plasma techniques developed for strongly magnetized, strongly coupled non-neutral plasmas: rotating-wall compression, evaporative and cyclotron cooling, and plasma-mode diagnostics.

name: Electroweak magnetogenesis as a dynamo seed
summary: Gradients of the Higgs-field phase during electroweak symmetry breaking can generate magnetic fields (Vachaspati 1991), and helical fields from the electroweak or QCD epochs inverse-cascade to larger scales. This is a primordial alternative to the Biermann battery for seeding galactic and cluster dynamos.
breaks: With m_H = 125 GeV the Standard-Model electroweak transition is a smooth crossover, which weakens bubble-collision magnetogenesis. The surviving field strengths and coherence lengths may also be too small without strong amplification.
sources: Parker (1955). "Hydromagnetic Dynamo Models". *Astrophys. J.* 122, 293. [doi:10.1086/146087](https://doi.org/10.1086/146087)

name: Plasmon mass and the Anderson–Higgs mechanism
summary: Transverse electromagnetic waves in a plasma obey ω² = ω_p² + c²k², the dispersion of a massive (Proca) photon. Anderson (1963) used the plasmon and the Meissner effect to argue that a gauge field can gain mass without losing gauge invariance by absorbing the would-be Goldstone mode. Englert–Brout and Higgs made the idea relativistic in 1964, and it gives the W and Z their masses.
breaks: The plasma mass belongs to a thermal medium in a preferred frame (longitudinal and transverse modes differ) and involves no spontaneously broken symmetry: a normal plasma does not screen static magnetic fields. The electroweak mass comes from a Lorentz-invariant vacuum condensate, as in a superconductor's Meissner effect.
sources: Englert & Brout (1964). "Broken Symmetry and the Mass of Gauge Vector Mesons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 321. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321)
Higgs (1964). "Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508)

name: Colour Debye screening in the quark–gluon plasma
summary: Free colour charges in the quark–gluon plasma screen chromoelectric fields as electrons and ions screen a test charge, with Debye mass m_D ~ gT. Once the screening length falls below a quarkonium radius the heavy-quark pair unbinds (Matsui–Satz J/ψ suppression), and lattice Polyakov-loop correlators measure the screening.
breaks: Chromomagnetic fields are screened only non-perturbatively, at g²T. The coupling is not small near T_c, so perturbative m_D is unreliable, and the plasma is non-abelian, relativistic and quantum.

name: Strongly coupled QGP and strongly coupled Coulomb plasmas
summary: The near-perfect-fluid QGP invited comparison with classical strongly coupled plasmas. A coupling parameter Γ (potential over kinetic energy) of order 1–10 puts the sQGP in the liquid range of one-component and Yukawa plasmas. Classical colour molecular dynamics borrowed from OCP simulations reproduces liquid-like transport, and in both systems shear viscosity is lowest near the liquid–gas crossover.
breaks: The QGP is relativistic and quantum (its η/s ≈ 1/4π sits near a conjectured quantum bound with no classical analogue), non-abelian with confinement, and has a running coupling. Dusty plasmas are classical, abelian and strongly damped by neutral gas.
sources: Thomas et al. (1994). "Plasma Crystal: Coulomb Crystallization in a Dusty Plasma". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 73, 652. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.652](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.652)

name: Hard thermal loops are non-abelian Vlasov theory
summary: The leading soft-field response of a hot gauge plasma is the hard-thermal-loop effective action of Braaten–Pisarski and Frenkel–Taylor. Linearized Vlasov equations for hard colour-charged quasiparticles reproduce it exactly (Blaizot–Iancu; Kelly, Liu, Lucchesi & Manuel), including gluon plasmons with ω_pl = m_D/√3, Debye screening and Landau damping of space-like (ω<k) gluons.
breaks: Covariant derivatives make the Vlasov equation non-abelian (colour precession, Wong equations). Beyond leading order, collisions and the soft magnetic scale g²T require Bödeker's effective theory or the lattice.
sources: Malmberg & Wharton (1964). "Collisionless Damping of Electrostatic Plasma Waves". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 184. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.184](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.184)

name: Chromo-Weibel instability and QGP isotropization
summary: A quark–gluon plasma with an anisotropic momentum distribution, as produced early in heavy-ion collisions, is unstable to magnetic-type Weibel/filamentation modes, just as anisotropic electron plasmas are (Mrówczyński; Romatschke–Strickland; Arnold, Lenaghan & Moore 2003). The chromo-Weibel instability speeds isotropization in weak-coupling bottom-up thermalization.
breaks: Non-abelian self-interaction changes saturation: growth feeds a cascade to the ultraviolet rather than saturating as in an abelian plasma. At RHIC/LHC couplings its role relative to strong-coupling (holographic) isotropization is debated.

name: Axion searches as quantum sensing
summary: Axion dark matter is hunted with quantum sensors. Haloscopes convert axions into microwave photons at ν=m_ac²/h, read by near-quantum-limited Josephson amplifiers and by squeezed-state receivers that beat the standard quantum limit. Spin-precession experiments (CASPEr, magnetometer networks) look for the axion field acting as an oscillating pseudo-magnetic field on spins.
map: \mathcal{L}_{a\gamma}=g_{a\gamma\gamma}\,a\,\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B,\quad h\nu=m_ac^2,\quad H_{aN}\propto g_{aN}\nabla a\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma
sources: Budker & Romalis (2007). "Optical magnetometry". *Nature Phys.* 3, 227. [arXiv:physics/0611246](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0611246)
Degen, Reinhard & Cappellaro (2017). "Quantum sensing". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 89, 035002. [arXiv:1611.02427](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.02427)

name: Skipper CCDs: semiconductor detectors for sub-GeV dark matter
summary: Sub-GeV dark matter scattering on electrons leaves only a few eV. SENSEI and DAMIC-M use skipper CCDs that read each pixel's charge many times to reach sub-electron noise. Silicon's band gap and pair-creation energy set the threshold, and leakage current and spurious charge are the backgrounds.

name: Tabletop force sensors test sub-millimetre gravity
summary: Large extra dimensions (ADD) and light moduli predict Yukawa-like departures from Newton's inverse-square law below ~1 mm. Precision force sensors bound the strength–range (α, λ) plane: torsion balances, and increasingly atom interferometers and levitated or mechanical quantum sensors.
sources: Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos & Dvali (1998). "The hierarchy problem and new dimensions at a millimeter". *Phys. Lett. B* 429, 263. [arXiv:hep-ph/9803315](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9803315)

name: Magic momentum: storage-ring dynamics for g−2
summary: Muon g−2 rings run at the magic momentum (γ≈29.3, p≈3.09 GeV/c), where electrostatic-quadrupole focusing drops out of the Thomas–BMT spin precession. Residual betatron oscillations, momentum spread and pitch corrections are the beam-dynamics systematics. J-PARC's planned design instead uses an ultra-cold, low-emittance beam with no electric focusing.

name: Muon g−2 as precision spin-precession magnetometry
summary: Muon g−2 measures an anomalous spin-precession frequency ω_a against a storage-ring field mapped at the ~0.1 ppm level or better. The field comes from pulsed proton-NMR probes calibrated to shielded-proton standards, the same phase-accumulation principle used in NMR and atomic magnetometers. Electron g−2 uses single-electron quantum-jump spectroscopy in a Penning trap.

name: Colliders as accelerator-physics machines
summary: Every collider measurement depends on a machine designed with accelerator physics. Magnets and RF set the energy frontier, and luminosity sets the event rate, so a process with cross section σ gives events at rate Lσ. The main collider design choices (hadron vs lepton beams, circular vs linear) are accelerator-physics trade-offs.

name: CLOUD: accelerator beams test aerosol nucleation
summary: CERN's CLOUD experiment uses a Proton Synchrotron beam as an adjustable cosmic-ray source in an ultra-clean chamber to measure ion-induced nucleation of atmospheric aerosols. It showed that ions boost nucleation from sulphuric-acid and organic vapours. The proposed cosmic-ray–cloud–climate link is contested, and CLOUD's own modelling finds it too weak to explain recent warming.

name: Magnet and SRF technology set future-collider reach
summary: Accelerator hardware bounds future-collider designs. A ~100 TeV FCC-hh needs ~14–16 T Nb₃Sn or HTS dipoles. FCC-ee, CEPC and ILC rely on high-Q niobium SRF cavities, and CLIC relies on 70–100 MV/m normal-conducting X-band structures. In practice, magnet and cavity R&D decides collider strategy.
sources: Padamsee (2017). "50 years of success for SRF accelerators—a review". *Supercond. Sci. Technol.* 30, 053003. [doi:10.1088/1361-6668/aa6376](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6668/aa6376)

name: Muon ionization cooling evades Liouville
summary: Muons are produced with large emittance and live 2.2 μs, so a muon collider needs ionization cooling. Energy loss in absorbers removes momentum in all directions, and RF restores only the longitudinal part, so emittance shrinks. Dissipation evades Liouville's theorem, with multiple scattering as the heating term. MICE demonstrated the effect.

name: Synchrotron radiation: collider loss, light-source product
summary: Light sources turn relativistic Larmor radiation into X-ray beams, and the same radiation is the energy-loss limit of circular e⁺e⁻ colliders. The loss per turn scales as γ⁴/ρ. That is why FCC-ee and CEPC need ~90–100 km rings, why linear colliders are proposed, and why a muon collider radiates (m_e/m_μ)⁴ less.

name: CLIC X-band structures for VHEE FLASH therapy
summary: High-gradient X-band accelerating structures developed for CLIC are being adapted into compact very-high-energy-electron (VHEE, ~100–200 MeV) machines, for example by the CERN–CHUV collaboration. These could deliver ultra-high-dose-rate FLASH radiotherapy to deep tumours.

name: Dipole field sets the LHC energy
summary: In a fixed tunnel the dipole field sets the beam momentum. 8.33 T Nb–Ti dipoles at 1.9 K on a ~2.8 km bending radius give the design 7 TeV per beam. HL-LHC brings in Nb₃Sn magnets of the 11–12 T class, and hadron colliders beyond it are limited by magnet technology.

name: LHC luminosity from emittance and beta*
summary: LHC luminosity is a beam-dynamics quantity. The beam size at the interaction point is σ*=√(εβ*), so luminosity rises with bunch intensity and falls with emittance and β*. Beam–beam tune shifts, crossing-angle geometry and pile-up limit how far it can be pushed, which is the HL-LHC problem.
sources: Courant & Snyder (1958). "Theory of the alternating-gradient synchrotron". *Ann. Phys.* 3, 1. [doi:10.1016/0003-4916(58)90012-5](https://doi.org/10.1016/0003-4916(58)90012-5)

name: Superconducting magnet industry: Tevatron to MRI
summary: Clinical MRI uses liquid-helium-cooled Nb–Ti superconducting solenoids, the same conductor technology as hadron-collider dipoles. The Tevatron, the first large superconducting synchrotron, helped create the industrial Nb–Ti cable production behind whole-body MRI magnets. LHC-era Nb₃Sn and HTS development now feeds high-field MRI.

name: Symmetry-aware networks for jets and protein structures
summary: Both fields learn from point clouds whose physics has exact symmetries. Jet tagging uses Lorentz-equivariant graph networks, and AlphaFold 2 uses SE(3)-invariant point attention, so each builds the symmetry into the architecture. Diffusion and flow generative models are used both for fast detector simulation and for protein design.
sources: Jumper et al. (2021). "Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold". *Nature* 596, 583. [doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2)

name: Hybrid pixel detectors from LHC trackers to X-ray beamlines
summary: Hybrid pixel detectors built for LHC tracking (CMS pixel R&D at PSI, the Medipix/Timepix chips) became the noise-free single-photon-counting X-ray detectors, such as PILATUS and EIGER, that now dominate synchrotron diffraction. FEL pulses need integrating detectors instead, because every photon arrives within femtoseconds.

name: Silicon trackers are reverse-biased p–n diodes
summary: Silicon strip and pixel trackers are fully depleted p–n junctions read out by CMOS electronics, so tracker design is device physics: depletion voltage, leakage current, and radiation-induced change of effective doping. Monolithic active pixel sensors such as ALICE ITS2 grew out of commercial CMOS image sensors, and LGADs add avalanche gain for timing.

name: Muography images geological interiors with cosmic muons
summary: Cosmic-ray muon detectors built from particle-physics technology (scintillators, emulsions, gaseous chambers) measure how much muons are attenuated through volcanoes, mountains and pyramids. The result is a map of density times path length that complements seismic tomography for near-surface structure.

name: Photon-counting pixel detectors for spectral CT
summary: Hybrid pixel readout chips from the CERN-hosted Medipix collaboration count single X-ray photons against energy thresholds. Used in CT, they give energy-resolved (spectral) images that separate tissues and contrast agents. Medipix-based MARS scanners have imaged humans, and photon-counting CT is now entering clinical use.

name: Scintillators, SiPMs and timing shared by HEP and TOF-PET
summary: A PET scanner is a coincidence-counting particle detector. Dense fast scintillators (LSO/LYSO, studied by CERN's Crystal Clear collaboration), photodetectors from PMTs to SiPMs, and picosecond timing move between the fields in both directions. TOF-PET's ~200 ps coincidence timing informed HEP crystal timing layers such as CMS LYSO+SiPM, and HEP timing R&D now aims at PET.
sources: Ter-Pogossian et al. (1975). "A Positron-Emission Transaxial Tomograph for Nuclear Imaging (PETT)". *Radiology* 114, 89. [doi:10.1148/114.1.89](https://doi.org/10.1148/114.1.89)

name: Bethe stopping power: dE/dx tagging and the Bragg peak
summary: Detectors use the Bethe formula to identify particles by ionization energy loss, and the same formula gives charged-particle therapy its Bragg peak. Wilson proposed proton therapy on this basis. HEP transport codes such as Geant4 and FLUKA are now standard for therapy dose calculation.
sources: Wilson (1946). "Radiological Use of Fast Protons". *Radiology* 47, 487. [doi:10.1148/47.5.487](https://doi.org/10.1148/47.5.487)

name: Geoneutrinos measure Earth's radiogenic heat
summary: Antineutrinos from the U and Th decay chains, detected by inverse beta decay in KamLAND and Borexino (soon JUNO), directly measure radiogenic heat production in the crust and mantle. This complements seismic Earth models such as PREM on the question of what powers mantle convection and the geodynamo. ⁴⁰K antineutrinos are below the detection threshold.
sources: Dziewonski & Anderson (1981). "Preliminary reference Earth model". *Phys. Earth Planet. Inter.* 25, 297. [doi:10.1016/0031-9201(81)90046-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9201(81)90046-7)

name: SQUID-read microcalorimeters for neutrino mass
summary: Calorimetric neutrino-mass experiments embed ¹⁶³Ho in metallic magnetic calorimeters read by SQUIDs (ECHo) or in transition-edge sensors (HOLMES) to measure the electron-capture endpoint. This complements KATRIN's tritium spectrometer. Project 8 measures tritium β energies from the frequency of their cyclotron radiation.
sources: KATRIN Collaboration (2022). "Direct neutrino-mass measurement with sub-electronvolt sensitivity". *Nature Phys.* 18, 160. [arXiv:2105.08533](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.08533)

name: MSW resonance as a Landau–Zener crossing
summary: Solar-neutrino flavour conversion is a two-level avoided crossing swept by the density gradient. It follows the same Landau–Zener hopping formula that governs nonadiabatic transitions between molecular potential-energy surfaces. Adiabatic MSW conversion is the case where the system stays on one adiabatic surface.
breaks: In molecules the crossing coordinate is a nuclear degree of freedom with its own dynamics and back-reaction, often multidimensional, with conical intersections and geometric phases. For neutrinos the solar density profile fixes the sweep and there is no back-reaction.
sources: Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)

name: Neutrino oscillation tomography of Earth's core
summary: Atmospheric neutrinos crossing the Earth feel an MSW matter potential set by the electron density, which seismology supplies through PREM. Turned around, future oscillation measurements and IceCube absorption data weigh the core and mantle without seismic waves. They could also constrain the core's composition through its Z/A.
sources: Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)
Dziewonski & Anderson (1981). "Preliminary reference Earth model". *Phys. Earth Planet. Inter.* 25, 297. [doi:10.1016/0031-9201(81)90046-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9201(81)90046-7)

name: Instanton theory of tunnelling reaction rates
summary: Field theory uses a Euclidean saddle point (the instanton or bounce) for theta-vacuum tunnelling and false-vacuum decay. Chemistry uses the same saddle point in semiclassical and ring-polymer instanton rate theory for hydrogen-atom and proton-transfer tunnelling. It explains large kinetic isotope effects and low-temperature interstellar chemistry.
map: k\simeq A\,e^{-S_E[\bar x]/\hbar},\quad S_E=\int d\tau\left[\tfrac12m\dot x^2+V(x)\right]
breaks: Chemical instantons are periodic orbits on a multidimensional nuclear potential surface with no topological charge. Gauge-theory instantons are classified by winding number and act on field configurations.

name: Ring polymers: imaginary-time path integrals for nuclei
summary: Wick rotation turns a quantum particle's partition function into a classical ring polymer of P beads, the same Euclidean discretization that underlies lattice field theory. Path-integral molecular dynamics and ring-polymer rate theories use it to include zero-point energy and tunnelling of light nuclei in reactions.

name: Coupled cluster: field-theory diagrams in chemistry
summary: Coupled-cluster theory, now quantum chemistry's gold standard as CCSD(T), was brought into chemistry by Čížek using quantum-field-theory tools. These were second quantization, Goldstone/Feynman-type diagrams, and the linked-cluster theorem that guarantees size extensivity. The exponential ansatz itself came from nuclear many-body theory.
sources: Čížek (1966). "On the Correlation Problem in Atomic and Molecular Systems. Calculation of Wavefunction Components in Ursell-Type Expansion Using Quantum-Field Theoretical Methods". *J. Chem. Phys.* 45, 4256. [doi:10.1063/1.1727484](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1727484)

Raghavachari et al. (1989). "A fifth-order perturbation comparison of electron correlation theories". *Chem. Phys. Lett.* 157, 479. [doi:10.1016/S0009-2614(89)87395-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0009-2614(89)87395-6)

name: PET runs on QED pair annihilation
summary: PET imaging uses the QED process e⁺e⁻→γγ: annihilation at rest gives two 511 keV photons almost back-to-back, and the pair's leftover momentum adds a small acollinearity. Positrons often form positronium first. Its para (2γ) and ortho (3γ) states have tissue-dependent lifetimes, which positronium-lifetime imaging is starting to use.
sources: Ter-Pogossian et al. (1975). "A Positron-Emission Transaxial Tomograph for Nuclear Imaging (PETT)". *Radiology* 114, 89. [doi:10.1148/114.1.89](https://doi.org/10.1148/114.1.89)

name: Geometric phase at conical intersections as a gauge field
summary: Adiabatically eliminating the electrons leaves the nuclei moving in a Berry connection. Around a conical intersection the electronic wavefunction changes sign, a molecular Aharonov–Bohm flux that changes vibronic spectra and reaction product distributions. Degenerate electronic manifolds give a non-abelian (Wilczek–Zee) connection with the structure of a Yang–Mills potential.
map: \mathbf A_{mn}(\mathbf R)=i\langle m(\mathbf R)|\nabla_{\mathbf R}n(\mathbf R)\rangle,\quad\oint\mathbf A\cdot d\mathbf R=\pi
breaks: The gauge field is emergent and kinematic. It has no Yang–Mills kinetic term or dynamics of its own, its gauge freedom is just the phase choice of the electronic states, and it exists only within the adiabatic approximation.

name: Quantum-computing targets: lattice gauge theories and molecules
summary: On classical computers, lattice QCD at finite density or in real time runs into the fermion sign problem, and strongly correlated molecules run into exponential Hilbert-space growth. Both are therefore flagship quantum-computing applications. They share fermion-to-qubit encodings, Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation, variational eigensolvers and phase estimation.

name: Membrane bending rigidity runs like an asymptotically free coupling
summary: Thermal undulations make a fluid membrane's bending rigidity fall logarithmically with length scale, just as the coupling of the asymptotically free 2D nonlinear sigma model runs. The membrane persistence length plays the role of the dynamically generated mass gap.
breaks: The fluctuations are thermal, not quantum, and early work disputed the prefactor of the logarithm. Lipid bilayers with κ≈10–20 k_BT have astronomically long persistence lengths, so real membranes never reach the crumpled, confinement-like regime.
sources: Helfrich (1973). "Elastic Properties of Lipid Bilayers: Theory and Possible Experiments". *Z. Naturforsch. C* 28, 693. [doi:10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209](https://doi.org/10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209)
Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)

name: Electron EDM searches in polar molecules
summary: CP violation beyond the Standard Model would give the electron an electric dipole moment. Heavy polar molecules (ThO, HfF⁺, YbF) amplify it with internal effective fields of order 10–100 GV/cm. Precision molecular spin-precession spectroscopy therefore bounds new CP-violating physics at multi-TeV scales and constrains electroweak baryogenesis.

name: Stochastic cooling enabled the W and Z discovery
summary: Van der Meer's stochastic cooling senses a beam's fluctuations with a pickup and corrects them with a kicker. It made dense antiproton beams possible for CERN's SppS collider, where UA1 and UA2 found the W and Z in 1983 and directly confirmed electroweak theory.
sources: van der Meer (1985). "Stochastic cooling and the accumulation of antiprotons". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 57, 689. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.57.689](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.57.689)

name: Parity violation in chiral molecules
summary: Z-boson exchange between electrons and nuclei should give the two mirror-image forms of a chiral molecule slightly different energies. This parity-violating energy difference is predicted to be tiny and has never been measured spectroscopically. Its proposed role in seeding biological homochirality is contested.
map: H_{\rm PV}\propto G_F\,Q_W\{\boldsymbol\sigma_e\cdot\mathbf p_e,\delta^3(\mathbf r)\},\quad Q_W\approx Z(1-4\sin^2\theta_W)-N

name: Born–Oppenheimer picture of quarkonium hybrids
summary: Heavy-quark hybrids and some tetraquarks are treated like diatomic molecules. The slow heavy quark–antiquark pair plays the nuclei and the gluon and light-quark fields play the electrons. Lattice static potentials carry diatomic term symbols (Σ_g⁺, Π_u, …), and the heavy pair vibrates on them (Born–Oppenheimer EFT).
breaks: The scale separation is modest: gluonic excitation gaps are not much larger than charmonium level spacings. The light fields carry colour and confine, and spin and recoil corrections are much larger than in molecules.
sources: Born & Oppenheimer (1927). "Zur Quantentheorie der Molekeln". *Ann. Phys.* 389, 457. [doi:10.1002/andp.19273892002](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19273892002)
